subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

He__ goes hard with__ one and all.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. 'To be difficult'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"goes hard with"** means to be harsh, severe, or difficult in dealing with someone. (किसी के साथ सख्त या कठिन होना)

 
 
• **Example: **The teacher goes hard with students who do not complete their homework on time.
 
 
 
• **"To be difficult" **refers to something that is not easy to do, understand, or deal with. (कठिन होना)
 
 
• **Example: **Learning a new language can be difficult for many people.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the idiom "goes hard with one and all" means "to be difficult" with everyone.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. 'To be difficult'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To be busy over trifles** (छोटी-छोटी बातों में व्यस्त रहना): Spending time on unimportant or trivial matters.

 
 
• **Example:** He often gets busy over trifles and misses important deadlines.
 
 
 
• **To remain neutral** (तटस्थ रहना): Not taking sides in a conflict or dispute.
 
 
• **Example: **The mediator remained neutral throughout the negotiations.
 
 
 
• **To be unreliable** (अविश्वसनीय होना): Not dependable or trustworthy.
 
 
• **Example:** His constant delays make him an unreliable team member.
 
 

179:Tbdb,
The correct answer is **Option 2**.
